Real Estate Department Overview:

Real Estate (RE) provides real estate services for the UC San Diego campus investment portfolio of University-owned and leased property valued in excess of $1.2 billion. The RE department is responsible for negotiating and implementing public/private partnership development projects, property acquisitions and dispositions, on-campus leasing to third parties including retail and research tenants, and off-campus leasing as landlord and as tenant. RE is a comprehensive real estate organization whose objectives are to complete real estate transactions on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of its clients and as a fiduciary for The Regents. The office comprises functional units that include leasing as landlord and as tenant, licenses, fiscal management and administrative services, property acquisitions and dispositions, public-private partnership development and asset management.

Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Finance and Administration (VCFA), the Executive Director of Real Estate is responsible for directing the operations of a complex real estate management department. The Executive Director leads change through strategic planning, designing and implementing real estate information systems, and overseeing significant real estate transactions and acquisitions, including public-private partnerships, leasing, property and asset management, new construction, and asset improvements. The position participates with senior leadership to establish strategic plans, master plans, and short- and long-term objectives that support organizational goals. The Executive Director makes strategic decisions impacting the organization and represents Real Estate Management on cross-functional teams and with community and/or professional organizations and societies.

The Executive Director of Real Estate is accountable for all real property acquisitions and divestitures, ground leases, leases, licenses, easements, and asset management activities. The position serves as a consultant and advisor to the Vice Chancellor, Chancellor, and other University officials on matters related to third-party development and leasing of University of California, San Diego land and facilities. The Executive Director also advises The Regents and the UC San Diego Foundation Board on matters related to gift and bequest real estate and serves as the staff representative to the Chancellor’s Real Estate Advisory Council.

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall real estate strategy of UC San Diego, which includes significant real estate interests across the main campus, the Hillcrest medical center campus, and off-campus locations. These holdings include investment properties, properties supporting medical purposes, housing, and other strategic university priorities. The Executive Director develops long-term strategies that support the academic mission of the University while engaging with multiple and complex stakeholders.

The Executive Director is also responsible for the planning and implementation of short-, mid-, and long-term faculty and staff housing initiatives for UC San Diego in support of the vision, mission, and strategic priorities of the University and its leadership.

Must possess excellent communication skills, including the ability to present, speak and effectively convince large and small groups, as well as the ability to be persuasive with the written word.
